title: Sono‐photochemical Division‐of‐Labor Synergy System for Selective Removal of Toluene and Preservation of Surfactants in Flushing Wastewater
content:
We propose a division-of-labor synergy system (DLSS) that couples ultrasound-driven micellar perturbation for enhanced mass transfer with UV-driven chemical activation of persulfate to achieve deep pollutant removal and surfactant retention.


ABSTRACT

Surfactant flushing is an effective technique for remediating toluene-contaminated soil, but it generates wastewater containing both toluene and surfactants, which poses a risk of secondary pollution. However, because toluene is sequestered within surfactant micelles, achieving both deep pollutant removal and efficient surfactant retention presents a dual challenge. Herein, we propose a division-of-labor synergy system (DLSS) that couples ultrasound-driven micellar perturbation for enhanced mass transfer with ultraviolet (UV, 254 nm)-driven chemical activation of persulfate to achieve deep pollutant removal and surfactant retention. In this process, ultrasound dynamically disrupts the micellar structure to expose the trapped toluene, whereas UV light at 254 nm continuously activates persulfate to generate sulfate radicals, thereby selectively oxidizing toluene without damaging the surfactant molecules. We achieve a toluene removal efficiency of 96.7% from the surfactant flushing wastewater, outperforming the compared systems for toluene oxidation, whereas the sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) retention rate exceeds 96.9%, which is essential for enabling surfactant reuse in subsequent soil flushing cycles and thus reducing both operational costs and secondary pollution. Response surface analysis reveals a significant interaction between ultrasound power and SDS concentration, as evidenced by the statistically significant interaction term in the fitted regression model, supporting that ultrasound functions essentially as a mass-transfer enhancer rather than a chemical activator in this system. This work offers a practical design strategy for the selective oxidation of pollutants in surfactant elution wastewater while achieving high surfactant retention.
